title: Checkpoint: Europe and Asia
objective: After this level you can describe the main mountains, rivers and regions of Europe and Asia.
summary: The Alpide belt runs from the Atlantic through the Mediterranean and the Himalayas to Indonesia. Continents crumple into fold mountains along it, and in Indonesia it meets the Ring of Fire.

cards.headline: One restless line runs from the Atlantic all the way to Indonesia.
cards.body: It passes the Mediterranean and the Himalayas, and it shakes. This chapter has been following it without saying so.

cards.headline: The Alpide belt
cards.body: Geologists call it the Alpide belt. It runs from the Atlantic through the Mediterranean region and the Himalayas to Java and Sumatra in Indonesia. Its mountains are the Alpine-Himalayan ranges: Level 62's Alps and Level 66's Himalayas are two beads on the same string. It's restless, too, producing about 17% of the world's largest earthquakes.

cards.headline: Crumple or dive
cards.body: Along this belt, plates push into Eurasia: a fragment of Africa behind the Alps, India behind the Himalayas. When continents meet like India and Asia, their rock has about the same density, so neither plate can slide under the other and the crust crumples upward. Compare Level 69's Ring of Fire, where one plate dives beneath another and helps make magma. Crumple, and you get fold mountains. Dive, and you get volcanoes.

cards.fact: In Indonesia, the Alpide belt meets the Ring of Fire.
cards.context: Two of the planet's great earthquake belts join up in one island country. Remember Level 69's volcanic zone running from Sumatra through Java? That's where this chapter's line finally reaches the Pacific's ring. Busy neighborhood.

mascot.line: Two earthquake belts shaking hands. Firmly. Very firmly.

cards.headline: Chapter 7 complete
learned: Why colliding continents crumple into mountains across Eurasia while diving plates feed volcanoes.
How a seasonal switch in the wind brings most of India's rain, and why harvests hang on it.
Why Asia's people crowd into a few regions while Siberia and the interior stay nearly empty.
What made China's Yellow River both the cradle of a civilization and a source of terrible floods.

questions.prompt: Which mountain ranges belong to the Alpide belt?

options.label: The Urals and the Scandinavian mountains
options.rationale: The belt runs along Eurasia's southern edge.

options.label: The Appalachians and the Great Dividing Range
options.rationale: Those are far from the belt.

questions.explanation: The Alpide belt's mountains are the Alpine-Himalayan ranges, from the Alps to the Himalayas.

questions.prompt: When India met Asia, why did the crust crumple instead of one plate sliding under?

options.label: The ocean between them was too deep
options.rationale: Depth wasn't the issue; density was.

options.label: India was moving too slowly
options.rationale: Speed didn't stop it sinking; density did.

options.label: Both had about the same rock density
Glaciers froze the two plates together
options.rationale: Ice has nothing to do with plate collisions.

questions.explanation: India and Asia have about the same rock density, so neither plate could slide under the other. The crust was thrust upward into the Himalayas instead.

questions.prompt: Which country from Level 69 is where the Alpide belt meets the Ring of Fire?

options.label: Japan
options.rationale: Japan is on the Ring of Fire, but the belts meet farther south.

options.label: The Philippines
options.rationale: On the ring, but not where the Alpide belt ends.

options.label: Russia
options.rationale: Russia is far north of the Alpide belt.

questions.explanation: The Alpide belt runs to Java and Sumatra in Indonesia, where it connects with the Ring of Fire.

questions.prompt: Kaliningrad and Kamchatka sit at Russia's far ends. From Level 64, how far apart are their clocks?

options.label: 24 hours
options.rationale: That would be a whole day.

questions.explanation: Kaliningrad and Kamchatka are 10 hours apart: 9:00 a.m. in one is 7:00 p.m. in the other.

questions.prompt: The Alpide belt runs through the Mediterranean. From Level 63, what are winters like there?

options.label: Freezing and snowy
options.rationale: Mediterranean winters are cool, not frozen.

options.label: Dry and dusty
options.rationale: Winter is the rainy season there.

questions.explanation: A Mediterranean climate has hot, dry summers and cool, wet winters.
